title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction for Surface Codes Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is indispensable for the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computers. Surface codes are a leading QEC architecture due to their high error thresholds and planar design. The core challenge lies in the decoding process: inferring latent physical errors from syndrome measurements and applying appropriate corrections. Although there are classical decoders, their performance can degrade with complex noise or be computationally demanding. This paper investigates an advanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approach, employing a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (DQN), to decode X-type Pauli errors on a$\mathbf{d}=\mathbf{3}$rotated surface code. The DRL agent leverages syndrome history to discern temporal error correlations and utilizes a multi-round correction strategy, enabling iterative refinement of corrective actions within an environment that simulates both physical qubit errors and syndrome measurement noise. After 30,000 training episodes with a 5 % physical error rate and 1 % measurement noise, the agent achieved a 0.00 % logical error rate in the extended test, an average episode reward of 0.38, and successfully cleared syndromes in 63 % of the test cases, demonstrating robust learning of a safe decoding policy. The persistent challenge of high training loss, despite good policy performance, is discussed, offering insights into value function approximation in complex QEC environments.

title: A Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Predictive Analytics in Distributed Healthcare Systems
abstract: Federated learning has become a groundbreaking structure in training smart healthcare designs without making sensitive patient information visible. This paper introduces a superior federated design that is aimed at refining prediction accuracy, enhancing privacy guarantees, minimizing communication load, and ensuring resilience in demanding non-IID clinical settings. The proposed model incorporates the concept of differential privacy, effective aggregation schemes, communication minimization through optimization, and personalization mechanisms to guarantee flexibility of the heterogenous healthcare facilities. It is based on the idea of differential privacy noise calibration that prevents leakage with model gradients and does not harm utility. Intense aggregation minimizes the impact of bad updates and targeted attacks, and thus, the integrity of the global model is high. title: A Hybrid Code-Mixed Sentiment Analysis Framework Integrating Rule-Based Sarcasm Detection, Emoji Emotion Modeling, and LLM-Driven Discourse Reasoning
abstract: The booming growth of the code-mixed content on social media platforms has exposed the vulnerability of the archetypal sentiment analysis systems, particularly in the poly-lingual mixing, sarcasm, colloquialism, and utilization of emojis to convey feelings. The paper proposes a Hybrid Code-Mixed Sentiment Analysis Framework, which combines transformer-based classification, rule-based sarcasm detection, emoji-based emotion modelling, and discourse reasoning based on large language models (LLM). The given system utilizes a multilingual XLM-RoBERTa-based primary sentiment classifier, with a heuristic sarcasm detector and emoji-to-emotion mapping layer to learn symbolic affective cues. An LLM component is used to conduct zero-shot discourse-level reasoning on the preprocessed inputs to add context and be more interpretable. It is scaled and reproducible with a FastAPI back-end and a Streamlit front end which is deployed in a modular manner. Experimental analysis shows that the hybrid architecture is more contextual and interpretable than standalone transformer-based models, which indicates the efficiency of integrating symbolic, statistical, and generative AI methods to perform robust code-mixed sentiment analysis.

title: Error analysis of translation outputs of the Siswati-English Linguistic Translation Tool
abstract: The development of machine translation (MT) systems for low-resourced languages in South Africa, such as Siswati, is crucial for bridging the linguistic divide between speakers of this language and English. Although MT systems for Siswati are available, there is a lack of studies that have assessed their translation outputs. This study evaluates the translation outputs of the Siswati-English Linguistic Translation Tool (SELTT), which translates from Siswati to English and vice versa. English texts from various secondary online open sources were collected and translated by the SELTT into Siswati. The automatically translated texts were then manually evaluated based on the Multidimensional Quality Metrics to identify errors in the outputs. The results show that, in some instances, the SELTT accurately translated texts into Siswati. However, translation errors such as omissions, mistranslations, spelling mistakes, incorrect capitalisation and untranslated words were identified in the outputs. This assessment provides necessary feedback to developers to refine and improve the performance of the SELTT.

title: PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents operating under organizational policies must comply with authorization constraints typically specified in natural language. In practice, such specifications inevitably contain ambiguities and logical or semantic gaps that cause the agent's behavior to systematically diverge from the true requirements. We ask: by letting an agent evolve its policy understanding through interaction and corrective feedback from pre-deployment testing, can it autonomously refine its interpretation to close specification gaps? We propose PolicyBank, a memory mechanism that maintains structured, tool-level policy insights and iteratively refines them -- unlike existing memory mechanisms that treat the policy as immutable ground truth, reinforcing "compliant but wrong" behaviors. We also contribute a systematic testbed by extending a popular tool-calling benchmark with controlled policy gaps that isolate alignment failures from execution failures. While existing memory mechanisms achieve near-zero success on policy-gap scenarios, PolicyBank closes up to 82% of the gap toward a human oracle.

title: Structure as Computation: Developmental Generation of Minimal Neural Circuits
abstract: This work simulates the developmental process of cortical neurogenesis, initiating from a single stem cell and governed by gene regulatory rules derived from mouse single-cell transcriptomic data. The developmental process spontaneously generates a heterogeneous population of 5,000 cells, yet yields only 85 mature neurons - merely 1.7% of the total population. These 85 neurons form a densely interconnected core of 200,400 synapses, corresponding to an average degree of 4,715 per neuron. At iteration zero, this minimal circuit performs at chance level on MNIST. However, after a single epoch of standard training, accuracy surges to over 90% - a gain exceeding 80 percentage points - with typical runs falling in the 89-94% range depending on developmental stochasticity. The identical circuit, without any architectural modification or data augmentation, achieves 40.53% on CIFAR-10 after one epoch. These findings demonstrate that developmental rules sculpt a domain-general topological substrate exceptionally amenable to rapid learning, suggesting that biological developmental processes inherently encode powerful structural priors for efficient computation.

title: Entanglement quantification with randomized measurements is maximally difficult
abstract: The certification of quantum systems is essential for emerging quantum technologies, particularly in quantum communication, networks, and distributed computing, where maintaining a common reference frame across distant nodes poses significant challenges. Reference frame independent approaches, such as randomized measurement schemes, offer a promising route by reducing experimental demands while granting access to basis-independent quantities, including entanglement. However, the efficiency of such schemes in measuring such local invariants has remained unclear. In this work, we determine the minimal number of measurement settings required to access all two-qubit invariants. We further demonstrate that entanglement certification necessarily involves the most demanding invariants, establishing it as a maximally difficult task. Our results reveal a fundamental hierarchy among invariants, with direct implications for experimental feasibility and theoretical understanding of quantum certification. Finally, we extend our analysis beyond bipartite systems by applying it to the Kempe invariant in three-qubit systems, improving known measurement protocols and providing a first step toward uncovering similar hierarchies in higher dimensions.

title: NTIRE 2026 Challenge on Video Saliency Prediction: Methods and Results
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the NTIRE 2026 Challenge on Video Saliency Prediction. The goal of the challenge participants was to develop automatic saliency map prediction methods for the provided video sequences. The novel dataset of 2,000 diverse videos with an open license was prepared for this challenge. The fixations and corresponding saliency maps were collected using crowdsourced mouse tracking and contain viewing data from over 5,000 assessors. Evaluation was performed on a subset of 800 test videos using generally accepted quality metrics. The challenge attracted over 20 teams making submissions, and 7 teams passed the final phase with code review. All data used in this challenge is made publicly available - https://github.com/msu-video-group/NTIRE26_Saliency_Prediction.

title: Discovering Novel LLM Experts via Task-Capability Coevolution
abstract: Frontier model developers aim to train models continually to possess emergent, diverse capabilities. To extend capabilities, the current pre-training and post-training paradigm requires manually starting training runs with static datasets or reward functions every time. Addressing this limitation, our work pursues the insight that open-endedness (via the coevolution of models and tasks) can discover models with increasingly novel skills in a single run. We introduce a new model development framework that extends coevolution to large language model (LLM) discovery, open-ended \textit{Assessment Coevolving with Diverse Capabilities} (AC/DC). AC/DC evolves both LLMs via model merging and natural language tasks via synthetic data generation. AC/DC discovers growing archives of LLMs that surpass the capabilities of larger LLMs while taking up less GPU memory. In particular, our LLM populations achieve a broader Coverage of expertise than other curated models or baselines on downstream benchmarks, without \textit{any} explicit benchmark optimization. Furthermore, AC/DC improves Coverage over time, continually innovates on tasks and models, and improves performance in multi-agent best-of-N selection. Our findings highlight the potential of coevolution as a means of discovering broader sets of capabilities from base LLMs. Overall, AC/DC brings us one step closer to a profoundly new paradigm of LLM development, where continual improvements to the diversity of model capabilities can be accelerated by leveraging existing models as stepping stones to increasingly powerful models.

title: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
abstract: Mobile agents powered by vision-language models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in automating mobile tasks, with recent leading models achieving a marked performance leap, e.g., nearly 70% success on AndroidWorld. However, these systems keep their training data closed and remain opaque about their task and trajectory synthesis recipes. We present OpenMobile, an open-source framework that synthesizes high-quality task instructions and agent trajectories, with two key components: (1) The first is a scalable task synthesis pipeline that constructs a global environment memory from exploration, then leverages it to generate diverse and grounded instructions. and (2) a policy-switching strategy for trajectory rollout. By alternating between learner and expert models, it captures essential error-recovery data often missing in standard imitation learning. Agents trained on our data achieve competitive results across three dynamic mobile agent benchmarks: notably, our fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL reach 51.7% and 64.7% on AndroidWorld, far surpassing existing open-data approaches. Furthermore, we conduct transparent analyses on the overlap between our synthetic instructions and benchmark test sets, and verify that performance gains stem from broad functionality coverage rather than benchmark overfitting. We release data and code at https://njucckevin.github.io/openmobile/ to bridge the data gap and facilitate broader mobile agent research.

title: Does Biological Connectome Topology Change Neural Network Behavior?
abstract: We ask whether the wiring topology of a real biological connectome, imposed as a fixed binary mask on a gradient-trained network, changes what that network can learn. The connectome is the complete Caenorhabditis elegans chemical synapse map: 448 nodes, 4,681 synapses, density 2.33%. We use the full adjacency matrix as-is, without cropping or tiling, so all topological properties of the connectome are preserved. Four conditions are compared across four tasks (digit classification, diabetes regression, two-moons, sequential digit recognition) and five random seeds: fully dense, randomly sparse at matched density, bio-topological, and magnitude-pruned (a sparse topology extracted from a trained dense network). On classification tasks, biological and random-sparse masks reach the same accuracy within statistical noise and both overfit less than the dense baseline. On regression and the recurrent task, the dense network wins, and again the two sparse conditions are indistinguishable from each other. The specific pattern of C. elegans connections adds nothing beyond matched random sparsity. We report this as a negative result with some care: it rules out wiring topology alone as a mechanism for computational advantage, but says nothing about what happens when topology is combined with biologically plausible learning rules, spiking dynamics, or dendritic computation. These are the subjects of the next stages of this project.

title: Axiom Monodromy Valuation
abstract: We prove two results sharing a common formal structure: the obstruction to lifting local consistency to global consistency when a boundary iscrossed. \textbf{Part I (Logical).} For any formal system $F_1$ and any strictly stronger extension $F_2$, the founding declaration of $F_2$ occurs at a point with non-trivial monodromy relative to $F_1$. This follows from G\"{o}del's second incompleteness theorem combined with the fibration structure of the FTT--Revelation boundary. Declaration is structurally necessary, not contingent. \textbf{Part II (Economic).} The aggregate valuation of the U.S.\ AI sector (${\sim}\$3\text{T}$) implicitly assumes that unit economics at the subscriber level are sustainable. Direct computation shows that heavy-user unit economics yield a loss-per-user of \$4{,}800--\$9{,}800 per month at current pricing. Break-even pricing per heavy user is \$5{,}000--\$10{,}000 per month---a 25--50$\times$ increase over current consumer pricing and squarely in the range of enterprise contract pricing. The attempt to analytically continue the aggregate-level balance-sheet solvency down to the subscriber silo therefore encounters two layered monodromy obstructions: a unit-economics obstruction ($\eta \in [0.02, 0.04]$ versus the required $\eta \geq 1$), and a product-market discontinuity (the path from consumer to enterprise pricing crosses a categorical market-segment boundary that cannot be traversed continuously). Together these obstructions constitute a valuation discontinuity that does not lift through the fibration of the capital structure. Both results are instances of the same categorical phenomenon: a section of a fibration that exists globally cannot always be restricted to a section over a subspace when the monodromy of the fibration is non-trivial.

title: The Paton Operator Calculus: Composition, Sequencing, and Admissible Execution Paths
abstract: This paper defines the Paton Operator Calculus, a structural framework governing how operators combine into admissible execution paths within the Paton System. Building on the Paton Operator Formalisation and Operator Set, this work establishes the rules of operator composition, sequencing, and chain validity under admissibility constraint. It formalises how systems execute step by step while preserving structural permission to continue. The framework introduces no new domain-specific laws and does not modify governing equations. It operates as a pre-theoretical layer determining when operator sequences remain admissible and when continuation must terminate. This paper is part of the Paton Operator Layer and is structurally linked with: - Operator Stability and Failure: Admissibility Breakdown Under Sequential Constraint - Admissible Operator Optimisation: Selection and Efficiency Within Constraint Boundaries Together, these define how systems execute, degrade, and select paths under constraint. title: Comparative Analysis of Quantum and Classical Computing: Performance, Error Rates, and Hybrid Architectures
abstract: Classical computing is approaching its physical limits, so quantum computing as an alternative model requires careful evaluation. This study compares various aspects of two systems by looking at formal algorithmic complexity, simulation-based comparisons with realistic noise models, quantitative meta-analysis, figuring out the difference between physical and logical error rates, and clearly defining contributions. A thorough study examined 24,100 papers published between 2015 and 2024 from leading scientific databases. A study of algorithmic complexity using Big-O notation confirmed that Shor's algorithm is faster than standard O(exp((64/9)²/³ (log N)²/³ (log log N)²/³)) by a super polynomial factor, Grover's algorithm is faster by a quadratic factor (O(√N) versus O(N)), and quantum simulation is faster by an exponential factor. There were Five quantum machines exhibited physical error rates ranging from 10⁻² to 10⁻⁵. Simulation-based testing revealed that the quantum advantage emerges above certain complexity thresholds: at extremely high complexity, quantum processing reached 10.3 μs versus 40.2 μs for classical computing, with better error resistance (2.3% for quantum vs. 5.9% for classical). Quantum computing has real benefits in terms of speed, mistake tolerance, and energy economy for problems that are too complicated to solve with traditional methods. However, significant challenges remain in scalability and workforce development. Hybrid quantum-classical models offer the most promising path to near-term practical benefits. On the other hand, the shift to postquantum security needs instant attention, regardless of when quantum hardware will be available.

There were Five quantum machines exhibited physical error rates ranging from 10⁻² to 10⁻⁵. Simulation-based testing revealed that the quantum advantage emerges above certain complexity thresholds: at extremely high complexity, quantum processing reached 10.3 μs versus 40.2 μs for classical computing, with better error resistance (2.3% for quantum vs. 5.9% for classical). Quantum computing has real benefits in terms of speed, mistake tolerance, and energy economy for problems that are too complicated to solve with traditional methods. However, significant challenges remain in scalability and workforce development. Hybrid quantum-classical models offer the most promising path to near-term practical benefits. On the other hand, the shift to postquantum security needs instant attention, regardless of when quantum hardware will be available.

title: Using Large Language Models for Social Determinants of Health Phenotyping: Systematic Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Social determinants of health (SDoH), encompassing factors such as employment status, housing instability, and transportation access, play a critical role in health outcomes, yet are seldom captured in structured form within electronic health records (EHRs). Relevant information is instead embedded in unstructured clinical notes, limiting its systematic use for identifying patients who may benefit from targeted social-work interventions. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potentially scalable approach to automated SDoH extraction, yet no comprehensive evaluation has examined how model family, usage paradigm, and task formulation jointly affect performance across benchmarks. OBJECTIVE This study aims to conduct a systematic evaluation of proprietary and open-weight LLMs for sentence-level SDoH phenotyping, comparing zero-shot prompting, few-shot in-context learning, supervised fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across a synthetic SDoH benchmark and real-world clinical notes from MIMIC-III. METHODS A diverse set of proprietary models (GPT-4o, GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5-Sonnet) and open-weight models (Phi-4-14B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, LLaMA3.3-70B, QwQ-32B, Mixtral-8×7B) were evaluated on two corpora: a synthetic SDoH test set and 5328 social-history–related clinical notes from MIMIC-III. The SDoH classification task covered six categories (employment status, housing, transportation, parental status, relationship status, and social support). Models were evaluated under four paradigms: zero-shot prompting, few-shot in-context learning, supervised fine-tuning, and RAG. Two task formulations were also examined—single-label versus multi-label prediction, and detection of any SDoH versus adverse SDoH only. RESULTS In zero-shot and few-shot settings, open-weight models of moderate size were competitive with or superior to proprietary baselines: Phi-4-14B achieved a macro-F1 of 0.91 on the synthetic test set in the adverse SDoH setting, exceeding GPT-4o (macro-F1 0.86), while Phi-4-14B and Qwen3-14B attained the highest macro-F1 on MIMIC-III for adverse SDoH (0.47). On MIMIC-III, GPT-5.2 in the zero-shot multi-label setting achieved the highest any-SDoH macro-F1 (0.68), while Claude-4.5-Sonnet in the few-shot setting achieved the highest adverse-SDoH macro-F1 (0.65), both exceeding FLAN-T5XL fine-tuned on gold-annotated data (0.57 and 0.53, respectively). Supervised fine-tuning substantially improved in-distribution performance (Phi-4-14B macro-F1: 0.99) but degraded performance on MIMICIII (macro-F1: 0.06), indicating a pronounced domain mismatch. Multi-label prompting improved any SDoH detection for 6 of 7 models on MIMIC-III but was counterproductive for adverse SDoH in smaller models. RAG improved MIMIC-III performance for Phi-4-14B and Qwen3-14B but reduced accuracy on the synthetic test set. CONCLUSIONS Open-weight LLMs of moderate size obtained performance competitive with proprietary models on both benchmarks and thus represent a viable, privacy-preserving alternative to proprietary models for SDoH phenotyping. Supervised fine-tuning on synthetic data achieves near-ceiling performance on controlled benchmarks but generalizes poorly to authentic clinical documentation, underscoring the continued need for domain-representative training data. Multi-label prompting and few-shot exemplars offer the most reliable gains on real-world clinical notes, providing practical guidance for deploying LLMs under clinical privacy and resource constraints.

title: Prediction of Heterogeneous Cyber Violence Against Women Using Machine Learning and SHAP Technique
abstract: Women may experience various forms of physical and psychological distress as a result of cyber violence. Cyber bullying, harassment, identity theft, non-consensual sharing of personal information, disseminating false information, and other threats were not taken into consideration by any machine learning-based heterogeneous cyber violence prediction system developed in earlier studies. Lack of data annotation, inadequate preprocessing, and management of the class imbalance problem, minimal accuracy, bad feature selection, and missing parameter tuning were among the problems with the earlier research. This study provides an ML-based multi-class cyber violence prediction system against women with ensemble feature selection, optuna-based hyper parameter tweaking, and SHAP-based interpretability in order to overcome the current constraints. With 95.93 percent accuracy, the suggested XGBoost model is chosen for cyber violence prediction. The proposed XGBoost model outperforms previous efforts by 1.6 percent in accuracy and 2.2 percent in F1 score.

title: Revolutionizing Colon Cancer Diagnosis: A Novel Vision Transformer and Bi-LSTM-Based Deep Learning Model
abstract: Colorectal cancer remains one of the most common causes of death due to malignant tumors globally and early diagnosis can be made via histopathological image analysis. A novel deep learning model (ViT-BiLSTM) is proposed that combines Vision Transformer (ViT) and Bidirectional Long ShortTerm Memory (Bi-LSTM) networks, to classify histopathological images of the colon cancer samples in an accurate manner. We use two public datasets for our work which are NCT-CRC-HE100 K and colon subset of LC25000. Data preprocessing: including resizing to$128 \times 128$pixel, normalization and augmentation procedures to make it more robust. Model evaluation is performed using 10-fold cross-validation method which lead to better performance measures. We also employ and explain the results of local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), so to address the interpretability challenge of using deep learning in clinical settings, which can help make our models more trusted. Experimental results show that an average accuracy of 98.10 % on NCT-CRC-HE-100K and an average accuracy of 97.30 % on LC25000 are obtained, with the corresponding F1-scores at 97.85 % and 97.30 %, revealing superiority over existing benchmarks. The method transforms the diagnosis of colon cancer into a highly accurate phenomenon with interpretability.

title: Cross-Layer Detection of Stealthy Side-Channel Attacks in Multi-Tenant Clouds with Statistical False-Positive Control
abstract: Virtualization and isolation mechanisms in multitenant cloud infrastructures are not sufficient to prevent microarchitectural side-channel attacks. Most existing detection approaches rely either on single-layer monitoring signals or on computationally heavy learning models, both of which limit practicality in production-scale cloud environments. In addition, many proposed systems focus primarily on improving classification accuracy without explicitly controlling false-positive rates, which reduces operational trust and deployability. This paper proposes a cross-layer detection framework for stealthy side-channel attacks in multi-tenant clouds. The approach integrates microarchitectural performance counters, hypervisor-level scheduling metrics, and timing-based workload features into a unified feature representation. To provide formal control over false-positive rates under benign workload conditions, the detection model is augmented with statistical calibration based on conformal prediction. The framework is evaluated on a virtualized multi-tenant testbed with co-resident benign and adversarial workloads, including cache timing and memory contention attacks. Experimental results indicate that cross-layer feature fusion improves robustness compared to single-layer baselines, while the calibration mechanism maintains bounded false-positive rates with limited impact on detection sensitivity. These results suggest that lowoverhead, statistically controlled side-channel detection is feasible in real-world cloud deployments.

title: Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation
abstract: Recent work on subliminal learning demonstrates that language models can transmit semantic traits through data that is semantically unrelated to those traits. However, it remains unclear whether behavioral traits can transfer in agentic systems, where policies are learned from trajectories rather than static text. In this work, we provide the first empirical evidence that unsafe agent behaviors can transfer subliminally through model distillation across two complementary experimental settings. In our primary setting, we construct a teacher agent exhibiting a strong deletion bias, a tendency to perform destructive file-system actions via an API-style tool interface, and distill it into a student using only trajectories from ostensibly safe tasks, with all explicit deletion keywords rigorously filtered. In our secondary setting, we replicate the threat model in a native Bash environment, replacing API tool calls with shell commands and operationalizing the bias as a preference for issuing chmod as the first permission-related command over semantically equivalent alternatives such as chown or setfacl. Despite full keyword sanitation in both settings, students inherit measurable behavioral biases. In the API setting the student's deletion rate reaches 100% (versus a 5% baseline) under homogeneous distillation; in the Bash setting the student's chmod-first rate reaches 30%-55% (versus a 0%-10% baseline), with the strongest transfer observed in large-to-small distillation. Our results demonstrate that explicit data sanitation is an insufficient defense, and behavioral biases are encoded implicitly in trajectory dynamics regardless of the tool interface.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI): Interpreting Black-Box Models
abstract: Artificial intelligence has quickly moved beyond research laboratories and into everyday decision-making in areas such as healthcare, finance, employment, and public safety. While these systems often achieve impressive accuracy, many operate as “black boxes,” offering decisions without clear explanations that people can understand or challenge. This paper explores why such opacity undermines trust, accountability, and fairness, and presents Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) as a practical response to this problem. It introduces key ideas behind XAI, including the difference between local and global explanations, and reviews widely used methods such as LIME and SHAP. Through real-world examples from criminal justice, public administration, and healthcare, the study shows how explanations can support ethical decision-making, legal responsibility, and effective human-AI collaboration. At the same time, it highlights the limits of current XAI approaches, emphasizing the need for careful use, critical evaluation, and stronger regulatory oversight.

title: A CLOUD BASED E-VOTING SYSTEM USING NIN AUTHENTICATION MECHANISM FOR ELECTORAL PROCESS IN NIGERIA
abstract: Lack of transparency has led to a failure to deliver voters assurance, agitations of suspicions and mistrust from opposition political parties. This has also led to fear of voter’s insecurity, secrecy and possibility of verified results with the electronic systems that corrupt the electoral process in Nigeria. The gap observed is one that could aid the economy, government; individual and corporate organizations to improve on the state of life and develop better working systems which cannot be overemphasized. Therefore, there is need to design a transparent, trusted and secured cloud based electronic voting system that will be used during elections in Nigeria. The proposed system was built using Dynamic System Development Methodology (DSDM), Java programming language was employed at the frontend while MYSQL was used as backend for relational database and SQLite Maestro for INEC admin backend. The built model was tested with a sample dataset collected from Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) office Port Harcourt. The proposed model was evaluated and performance ranking of testing voting results using parameters such as state, electorate, and turnout in percentages showed excellent system efficiency. The proposed model performed better than other existing models and showed that it can be used to achieve transparent and trusted result during and after the election.

title: Evaluating Whether AI Has Reached Human-Level Reasoning in Insurance Decision Making
abstract: This study evaluates whether artificial intelligence has reached human-level reasoning in insurance decision making. The research compares responses from AI systems and experienced human surveyors when presented with a technically invalid motor insurance claim. The case involved an impossible scenario where rust was observed on a plastic car bumper. Human experts immediately identified the flaw and rejected the case, while AI systems assumed the input was correct and continued reasoning based on policy rules. The findings highlight the concept of Garbage In Garbage Out (GIGO), showing that AI systems are highly dependent on input quality and lack real-world validation ability. The study concludes that AI has not yet achieved human-level reasoning and should be used with human supervision in critical decision-making processes.

title: Voice User Interfaces at the Intersection of Speech Recognition, NLP and HCI: A Systematic Review
abstract: Voice User Interfaces (VUIs) are increasingly shaping human-computer interaction (HCI) by integrating advances in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). This systematic review examines 28 studies published between 2020 and 2025, selected through the PRISMA framework to ensure relevance. The analysis highlights recent trends in VUI research showing significant improvements in ASR accuracy via end-to-end neural models and enhanced language understanding through transformer-based NLP approaches. On the HCI side studies emphasize usability, personalization and multimodal interaction aiming to make VUIs more intuitive and engaging. Despite these advances, challenges such as demographic bias, latency, privacy risks and cultural adaptation persist indicating the need for inclusive, secure and interdisciplinary solutions. Bibliometric analysis and keyword mapping further reveal emerging themes and research gaps. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive snapshot of the current VUI landscape and offers insights into designing next-generation conversational agents that are context-aware, accessible and capable of supporting richer, more human-like interactions.

title: Solar PV Power Generation Forecasting Using an Attention-Based Bidirectional LSTM Network
abstract: To provide the reliability and efficiency of the solar energy system. The solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation should be predicted accurately. The generation of solar power is not a linear process and it changes with time depending on the environmental factors. Therefore, it is quite difficult to forecast solar power production properly. We, in this regard, introduce a new hybrid deep learning (DL) model, SP-BiLSTM-ATT, a composite of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory model and Attention mechanism to forecast the solar power generation. The model proposed is tested with the help of a solar power generation dataset that has been acquired via the Kaggle data repository. The performance of the proposed model is correlated to the performance of other well-known regression models, such as Decision Tree (dt), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF) and standard LSTM model. The model proposed has a much greater accuracy when compared to the conventional models with an$R 2$which is 0.95. The fact that the precision of the suggested model was steadily increased in all the experiments validates the reliability of the model.

title: Silent Weight Corruption: Evaluating GPU Memory Fault Attacks on Deep Neural Networks and Designing Lightweight Integrity Defenses
abstract: Deep neural networks deployed on GPU-accelerated platforms heavily rely on the integrity of parameters stored in high-performance memory during inference. While adversarial input manipulation and training-time attacks have been extensively researched, there is comparatively less focus on inferencetime parameter corruption due to hardware-level faults. This paper looks at the security consequences in the presence of sparse bit-level weight corruption on deployed neural networks. We develop a controlled fault injection framework that simulates GPU memory bit flips during inference and study their effect on the model's behaviour. Using layer-wise sensitivity analysis, we identify architectural regions that are most affected by parameter perturbations. Our results show that while random corruption leads to gradual accuracy degradation, selectively guided corruption can increase the probability of targeted misclassification under a limited budget on faults. To this end, we propose a lightweight integrity monitoring mechanism based on statistical profiling of intermediate activations. Experimental evaluation on standard image classification models shows that the proposed approach is capable of detecting moderate corruption with limited computational overhead. The results provide a framework for further analysis at the intersection of machine learning and system-level security.

title: "Excuse me, may I say something..." CoLabScience, A Proactive AI Assistant for Biomedical Discovery and LLM-Expert Collaborations
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into scientific workflows presents exciting opportunities to accelerate biomedical discovery. However, the reactive nature of LLMs, which respond only when prompted, limits their effectiveness in collaborative settings that demand foresight and autonomous engagement. In this study, we introduce CoLabScience, a proactive LLM assistant designed to enhance biomedical collaboration between AI systems and human experts through timely, context-aware interventions. At the core of our method is PULI (Positive-Unlabeled Learning-to-Intervene), a novel framework trained with a reinforcement learning objective to determine when and how to intervene in streaming scientific discussions, by leveraging the team's project proposal and long- and short-term conversational memory. To support this work, we introduce BSDD (Biomedical Streaming Dialogue Dataset), a new benchmark of simulated research discussion dialogues with intervention points derived from PubMed articles. Experimental results show that PULI significantly outperforms existing baselines in both intervention precision and collaborative task utility, highlighting the potential of proactive LLMs as intelligent scientific assistants.

In this study, we introduce CoLabScience, a proactive LLM assistant designed to enhance biomedical collaboration between AI systems and human experts through timely, context-aware interventions. At the core of our method is PULI (Positive-Unlabeled Learning-to-Intervene), a novel framework trained with a reinforcement learning objective to determine when and how to intervene in streaming scientific discussions, by leveraging the team's project proposal and long- and short-term conversational memory. To support this work, we introduce BSDD (Biomedical Streaming Dialogue Dataset), a new benchmark of simulated research discussion dialogues with intervention points derived from PubMed articles. Experimental results show that PULI significantly outperforms existing baselines in both intervention precision and collaborative task utility, highlighting the potential of proactive LLMs as intelligent scientific assistants.

title: CoPA: Benchmarking Personalized Question Answering with Data-Informed Cognitive Factors
abstract: While LLMs have demonstrated remarkable potential in Question Answering (QA), evaluating personalization remains a critical bottleneck. Existing paradigms predominantly rely on lexical-level similarity or manual heuristics, often lacking sufficient data-driven validation. We address this by mining Community-Individual Preference Divergence (CIPD), where individual choices override consensus, to distill six key personalization factors as evaluative dimensions. Accordingly, we introduce CoPA, a benchmark with 1,985 user profiles for fine-grained, factor-level assessment. By quantifying the alignment between model outputs and user-specific cognitive preferences inferred from interaction patterns, CoPA provides a more comprehensive and discriminative standard for evaluating personalized QA than generic metrics. The code is available at https://github.com/bjzgcai/CoPA.

title: CoTEvol: Self-Evolving Chain-of-Thoughts for Data Synthesis in Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong mathematical reasoning when trained on high-quality Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that articulates intermediate steps, yet costly CoT curation hinders further progress. While existing remedies such as distillation from stronger LLMs and self-synthesis based on test-time search alleviate this issue, they often suffer from diminishing returns or high computing overhead.In this work, we propose CoTEvol, a genetic evolutionary framework that casts CoT generation as a population-based search over reasoning trajectories.Candidate trajectories are iteratively evolved through reflective global crossover at the trajectory level and local mutation guided by uncertainty at the step level, enabling holistic recombination and fine-grained refinement. Lightweight, task-aware fitness functions are designed to guide the evolutionary process toward accurate and diverse reasoning. Empirically, CoTEvol improves correct-CoT synthesis success by over 30% and enhances structural diversity, with markedly improved efficiency. LLMs trained on these evolutionary CoT data achieve an average gain of 6.6% across eight math benchmarks, outperforming previous distillation and self-synthesis approaches. These results underscore the promise of evolutionary CoT synthesis as a scalable and effective method for mathematical reasoning tasks.

title: Beyond Cooling II: Experimental Tests of Structural Feedback Constraints on Decoherence in Quantum Computing
abstract: This work proposes an experimental program to test whether structural feedback constraints influence decoherence independently of temperature reduction in quantum computing systems. Building on a structure-first framework in which decoherence is interpreted as a resolution failure, the paper outlines fixed-temperature experiments designed to isolate the roles of topology, coupling geometry, and feedback pathways. A primary test compares open-chain, symmetric ring (control), and asymmetric spiral qubit architectures using identical components under controlled conditions, with coherence time, phase stability, and error accumulation measured directly. The asymmetric spiral topology introduces directional, non-recursive coupling pathways, enabling a clear distinction between simple pathway closure and structurally constrained feedback. Additional experiments examine controlled versus minimal coupling, distributed feedback versus external error correction, and temperature dependence across structurally distinct architectures. These experiments provide a direct method for distinguishing between thermal-limited and feedback-limited models of decoherence. If validated, the results would establish structural architecture as an independent control axis for coherence in quantum systems, with implications for scalable quantum computing design.

title: MEDIAÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA NO ENSINO: UMA PROPOSTA EXPERIMENTAL NA EDUCAÇÃO BÁSICA
abstract: Este estudo aborda a mediação tecnológica no ensino por meio da Robótica Educacional, destacando sua relevância como ferramenta pedagógica na educação básica. A incorporação de tecnologias digitais no ambiente escolar tem promovido mudanças significativas nas práticas de ensino, favorecendo abordagens mais dinâmicas, interativas e centradas no estudante. Nesse contexto, a robótica se apresenta como um recurso capaz de integrar conhecimentos de áreas como Física, Matemática e Informática, contribuindo para a aprendizagem significativa e o desenvolvimento do raciocínio lógico. O trabalho tem como objetivo analisar o uso da robótica educacional de baixo custo como estratégia didática, por meio da construção e programação de sistemas de semáforo utilizando a plataforma Arduino. Foram desenvolvidos três experimentos principais: um sistema básico de semáforo para veículos, um semáforo com acionamento manual para travessia de pedestres e um sistema semafórico em interseção viária com funcionamento sincronizado. As atividades envolveram a montagem de circuitos eletrônicos em protoboard, utilização de LEDs, resistores e botões, além da programação no ambiente Arduino IDE. A metodologia adotada baseou-se na aprendizagem ativa, incentivando a participação dos estudantes na resolução de problemas, na formulação de hipóteses e na experimentação prática. Os resultados evidenciam que a utilização da robótica educacional favorece a compreensão de conceitos científicos e tecnológicos, além de estimular habilidades cognitivas e socioemocionais, como trabalho em equipe, autonomia e pensamento crítico. Conclui-se que a robótica educacional, especialmente quando associada a soluções de baixo custo, constitui uma alternativa viável para a inovação das práticas pedagógicas, contribuindo para a formação integral dos estudantes e para a aproximação entre teoria e prática no processo de ensino-aprendizagem.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model-Based Explainable Boosting Machine Analysis for Interpretation of State-of-Health Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Accurate prediction of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and energy storage systems. While machine learning (ML)-based models have demonstrated strong predictive performance, their limited interpretability remains a major challenge for deployment in safety-critical applications. Although explainable boosting machines (EBMs) provide an interpretable alternative through their additive structure, existing studies still rely on manual analysis of model outputs, which restricts scalability and reproducibility. To address this limitation, this study proposes a structured interpretation framework that integrates EBMs with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The proposed framework employs EBMs to generate SOH predictions along with global feature importance and variable-level score-density visualizations. These outputs are subsequently processed by an MLLM to perform automated interpretation at both global and variable levels, followed by aggregation, cross-validation, and generation of a unified interpretation report. Experiments were conducted on a lithium-ion battery degradation dataset and the EBM achieved competitive predictive performance compared to baseline ML models. In addition, the quality of the generated interpretations was evaluated using both an MLLM-as-a-Judge and a user study. The evaluation results show that the generated interpretations consistently achieved high scores, with average ratings exceeding 4.5 out of 5 across key criteria such as interpretation accuracy and faithfulness, as assessed by both independent MLLMs and domain experts. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables reliable and scalable interpretation of battery SOH prediction models, providing a practical solution for explainable artificial intelligence in battery health management.

title: Connecting AI , Explainability and Semantic in Animal Applications: A Scoping Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly adopted in animal‐related domains such as health monitoring, behaviour analysis and welfare assessment. However, concerns about the transparency and interoperability of AI outputs are rising. This scoping review investigates how AI and explainable AI (XAI) are applied in animal‐related systems and examines the role of semantic technologies in enhancing their interoperability. In this review, we followed PRISMA‐ScR guidelines and conducted five structured searches across ScienceDirect, Springer, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Web of Science. The searches targeted AI applications (S 1 ), XAI applications (S 2 ) and the use of semantic knowledge in AI (S 3 ) and XAI (S 4 ). Studies were screened, assessed using the QualSyst tool and selected based on Q1/Q2 SJR or CORE C–A* classification. A total of 21 review papers were selected for AI applications and 8 for XAI. No eligible papers were found regarding the use of semantics in AI or XAI. While explainability is gaining attention, it remains mostly limited to visual or statistical tools, lacking domain‐specific contextualization. We observed that AI is now pervasive in animal‐related research, yet XAI practices remain underdeveloped and lack semantic grounding. This gap calls for ontology‐based explainability to enhance trust, relevance and usability for both experts and non‐specialists.

title: Enhancing Cyber Threat Intelligence Using Transformer Models for Text Classification
abstract: As a response to the growing complexity of cyber attacks, this paper formulates a comprehensive methodology for the development of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) through text classification automation. Older rule-based approaches cannot keep up with evolving threats like malware, phishing, and ransomware, which call for top-shelf Natural Language Processing (NLP)techniques. This study investigates the application of Transformer-based models like BERT, RoBERTa, SecBERT, and DistilBERTinextracting deep contextual relationships from unstructured cybersecurity text data in an efficient manner. Experimental procedure involves precise data preprocessing, class imbalance addressed through oversampling with RandomOverSampler and employing a stratified data split approach for effective performance evaluation. Baseline Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTMs and BiLSTMs) are compared to fine-tuned Transformer models in the study. One of the key contributions is the development of an ensemble stacking model that opposes SecBERT and DistilBERT, leveraging their complementary abil-ities-SecBERT's domain expertise and DistilBERT's efficiency. Further, in this work, SHAP and LIME explainability techniques are combined to produce explainable insights intomodel decisionmaking critical in building trust as well as delivering actionable intelligence for cybersecurity analysts. This ensemble performed vastly with an incredible accuracy rate of 95.76% on the test set. This research offers a robust, understandable, and highly effective method for automating cyber threat detection with a robust standard for real-world application, particularly in resource-constrained environments.

title: Earthquake Magnitude Prediction Using Feature-Engineered Machine Learning Models in the South Asia Region
abstract: Predicting earthquake magnitude is a fundamental problem in seismology. Accurate earthquake magnitude prediction is important in the South Asia region due to dense population and high seismic vulnerability. Machine Learning (ML) offers promising results in magnitude prediction by analyzing patterns from historical seismic data. A dataset from the United States Geological Survey has been used in this work with custom filtering of the seismic events from only the South Asia region. Existing studies face challenges due to limited 'feature engineering and simplistic handling of missing values. To solve this, we propose a regression-based pipeline with hyperparameter tuning and systematic comparison of various imputation techniques. Data cleaning is performed using correlation analysis and feature engineering transformed descriptive text data into meaningful features. Missing values are handled by evaluating many imputation techniques including MICE, Catboost, LightGBM etc. MICE imputation worked best as it preserves the interdependencies between features by iteratively modeling each missing values using the others and produces more realistic values. After imputation, One-Hot encoding was applied to convert categorical data into numerical and scaled them. ML algorithms like Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, XGBoost, GradientBoost, SVR, NuSVR were applied. NuSVR with hyperparameter tuning performed best obtaining R2of 0.94, RMSE of 0.1 and 0.05 MAE. This study confirms the effectiveness of careful feature engineering for improving prediction accuracy. Our proposed approach demonstrates a reproducible and practical ML pipeline for earthquake magnitude prediction in South Asia which can be extended in future by implementing deep learning and explainable AI models.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Decision Support System for Personalized Immunosuppressive Treatment in Kidney Transplant Recipients
abstract: Kidney transplant is a life-saving procedure in the management of end-stage renal diseases. However, graft long-term survival entirely relies on the effective management of immunosuppressive medications. Inappropriate dosing of immunosuppressive drugs may result in either severe complications of graft rejection or drug-induced toxicity. This paper proposes an AI-driven framework to analyze immunosuppressive medication patterns in kidney transplant patients using their longitudinal clinical data. For patient risk level assessment, the proposed system integrates data preprocessing, temporal feature modeling, and deep learning-based classification to support clinical decision-making in adjusting immunosuppressive medications. Clinical parameters such as laboratory test results, medication dosage, and patient demographics are leveraged to represent the dynamic response of patients over time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model yields a classification accuracy of 96.4%, with significant reduction in misclassifying high-risk cases. Results showed that the proposed approach is effective, reliable, and suitable for supporting immunosuppressive therapy optimization in post-kidney transplant care.

title: A Unified Hardware-to-Decoder Architecture for Hybrid Continuous-Variable and Discrete-Variable Quantum Error Correction in LiDMaS+
abstract: We present an architecture-level hardware-to-logical-to-decoder execution stack for hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum error correction in LiDMaS+. Provider-native records are normalized into a single decoder IO contract and replayed under fixed controls across MWPM, UF, BP, and neural-MWPM. In a Xanadu case study using fixture inputs and sampled public datasets, replay integrity was complete: 108/108 fixture and 4000/4000 real-slice request-response lines, with zero request-parse errors, zero response-parse errors, and zero decoder-name mismatches. Under matched inputs, decoder behavior is clearly regime-dependent. For weighted fixture summaries, average flip count was 1.296 (MWPM), 1.296 (UF), 0.667 (BP), and 1.296 (neural-MWPM). For weighted real-data summaries, average flip count was 0.641 (MWPM), 0.741 (UF), 0.318 (BP), and 0.641 (neural-MWPM); corresponding nonempty-flip rates were 0.490, 0.490, 0.318, and 0.490. Across fixture data, BP reduced weighted correction volume by 48.6\% versus MWPM; across real slices, BP reduced weighted correction volume by 50.4\% versus MWPM and 57.1\% versus UF. Quality controls show the central interpretability tradeoff: BP is intervention-conservative but leaves higher residual burden, while MWPM-family decoders intervene more aggressively and clear more syndrome. Warning-no-syndrome rates remained decoder-invariant and dataset-driven (fixture weighted 0.259; real weighted 0.510), confirming preserved sparsity semantics from hardware input to logical correction. Re-running analysis stages reproduced identical SHA-256 artifacts, enabling deterministic study iteration. These results establish a practical benchmarking foundation for photonic GKP-oriented hardware programs where decoder policy must be selected as a function of operating regime.

title: ASGNet: Adaptive Spectrum Guidance Network for Automatic Polyp Segmentation
abstract: Early identification and removal of polyps can reduce the risk of developing colorectal cancer. However, the diverse morphologies, complex backgrounds and often concealed nature of polyps make polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images highly challenging. Despite the promising performance of existing deep learning-based polyp segmentation methods, their perceptual capabilities remain biased toward local regions, mainly because of the strong spatial correlations between neighboring pixels in the spatial domain. This limitation makes it difficult to capture the complete polyp structures, ultimately leading to sub-optimal segmentation results. title: CLion: Efficient Cautious Lion Optimizer with Enhanced Generalization
abstract: Lion optimizer is a popular learning-based optimization algorithm in machine learning, which shows impressive performance in training many deep learning models. Although convergence property of the Lion optimizer has been studied, its generalization analysis is still missing. To fill this gap, we study generalization property of the Lion via algorithmic stability based on the mathematical induction. Specifically, we prove that the Lion has a generalization error of $O(\frac{1}{Nτ^T})$, where $N$ is training sample size, and $τ>0$ denotes the smallest absolute value of non-zero element in gradient estimator, and $T$ is the total iteration number. In addition, we obtain an interesting byproduct that the SignSGD algorithm has the same generalization error as the Lion. To enhance generalization of the Lion, we design a novel efficient Cautious Lion (i.e., CLion) optimizer by cautiously using sign function. Moreover, we prove that our CLion has a lower generalization error of $O(\frac{1}{N})$ than $O(\frac{1}{Nτ^T})$ of the Lion, since the parameter $τ$ generally is very small. Meanwhile, we study convergence property of our CLion optimizer, and prove that our CLion has a fast convergence rate of $O(\frac{\sqrt{d}}{T^{1/4}})$ under $\ell_1$-norm of gradient for nonconvex stochastic optimization, where $d$ denotes the model dimension. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness of our CLion optimizer.

title: Enhanced Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Dengue Fever Prediction: A Rule Extraction Approach
abstract: Dengue fever poses a critical public health challenge worldwide, particularly in developing countries with laboratory-constrained healthcare systems. Existing methods show promise but are prone to overfitting, which can be mitigated by LSTM-based deep learning models. However, LSTM inherently lack interpretability, a major barrier to clinical adoption in disease prediction. This study bridges robustness and clinical interpretability by integrating rule extraction with LSTM for dengue fever prediction, using a Mendeley dengue fever dataset comprising 1,003 instances and 9 features, preprocessed with label encoding, simple imputation, and synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE).The LSTM algorithm is optimized using GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV and combined with G-REX for transparent generation, evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC AUC. All three LSTM variants, including Baseline, GridSearchCV, and RSCV (20 iterations), achieve 100% across Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC. However, G-REX rules deliver exceptional practical performance: 98.99% Accuracy, 98.53% Precision, 100% Recall, 99.26% F1-Score, and 99.09% ROC-AUC, while maintaining 93.3% fidelity to LSTM predictions, affirming medical validity. These findings position LSTM models as a strong reference standard for dengue classification, enabling resource-limited clinics to achieve high-quality diagnostics through transparent, rule-based support systems. This study can be strengthened in future by exploring other rule-extraction techniques and incorporating diverse, time-series datasets to enhance reliability, interpretability, and generalizability across varied clinical settings.

title: An Empirical Comparative Study of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Transformer Models for Text Classification
abstract: Text classification as a sentiment analysis, spam and document classification is an important task in Natural Language Processing (NLP). Recent developments of deep learning, and transformer-based models have contributed significantly to classifying accuracy. These models have difficulty meeting computational efficiency, inference latency, and interpretability criteria, and cannot be used in resource-constrained and real-time settings. The models are critically compared based on accuracy, computational efficiency and trade-offs on benchmark datasets in this paper. The results indicate that transformer models are much more accurate than other conventional concepts, but have a significant disadvantage of being computationally expensive, which severely limits their actual implementation. Also, XAI methods and fairness-conscious training approaches are required particularly when issues of transparency and fairness of the existing model emerge. New methods like zero-shot learning, few-shot learning, and self-supervised learning are promising directions to further improve generalization and flexibility of NLP models. Future studies must focus on identifying light, energy efficient NLP architecture that can achieve good accuracy, interpretability and scalability. This work fills the gaps between theory and practice, which is why it can be of interest to both academic researchers and practitioners in the industry.

title: Interpretable Multi Head Attention Sarcasm Detection in Bangla Text Using a BERT Model and Explainable AI
abstract: Sarcasm is the opposite of what you want to say especially to hurt an individual. The sarcasm in Bengali text, or informal syntax of social media, is quite hard to detect and Bengali Natural Language Processing resources are limited. Our deep learning model does a far better performance at sarcasm detection but it uses a pre-trained Bangla BERT encoder and it contains a multi-head attention (MHA) fusion layer. This evolutional design will allow our model to respect the finer-grained contextual information of our model and sub-word associations embracing either sarcasm or overstatement. The results of our experiments are a clear indication of the significant improvement of the proposed BERT + MHA model that achieved a remarkable accuracy of 79.29 that is a massive improvement of the initial BERT model. This is the detail of how the attention mechanism of multiple heads enables the model to capture the fine linguistic features of sarcastic Bangla. In addition to the accuracy, we emphasized the model explainability by using Layer Integrated Gradients (LIG). This method gives explainability as it focuses on the specific words that influence most on the prediction of sarcasm by the model.

title: Public Sentiment Analysis on the Interim Government of Bangladesh Using NLP
abstract: Public opinion is important for assessing government performance, especially during sensitive political transitions. With the rapid growth of social media, people are sharing their thoughts online more than ever, creating large amounts of unstructured text data. This paper offers a detailed sentiment analysis of public opinions about the Bangladesh Interim Government using Natural Language Processing (NLP). We collected Bengali-language comments from online sources and automatically labeled them as positive or negative using a pretrained multilingual transformer model, XLM-RoBERTa. To make a controlled comparison, we evaluated both classical machine learning models and transformer-based deep learning models. We applied character-level TF-IDF features with Logistic Regression and a Logistic Regression-XGBoost ensemble. For contextual representation learning, we fine-tuned BanglaBERT. The experimental results show that the TF-IDF-based Logistic Regression model had the highest accuracy at 86.5 %, outperforming both the ensemble and Bangla-BERT models on this specific and moderately sized dataset. These findings show that classical NLP techniques are still very effective for lowresource Bengali political sentiment analysis tasks. This study gives practical insights into public views on governance in Bangladesh and compares different NLP methods for sentiment analysis in the Bengali language.

title: Cyberbullying Classification for Multilingual Context Using Deep Learning
abstract: Detecting abusive language in the context of multilingual social media is a very sensitive issue, especially in the case with Indian languages, where code-mixing and linguistic diversity are not an exception. In this paper, a comparative analysis of three deep learning models will be performed, namely an optimized Multilingual BERT (mBERT), XLM-RoBERTa, and a CNN-BiLSTM model with Attention, evaluated on a dataset of the MACD (Multilingual Abusive Comment Dataset) comprising of text in five of the major Indian languages. The same preprocessing pipeline was used to have uniformity in all the models. The experimental results indicate clearly that transformer-based models are much better than the traditional sequence architectures. In their turn, mBERT showed the best performance with the accuracy of 86.08 % and the macro-F1 of 0.860, closely matched with XLM-RoBERTa, which has the macro-F1 of 0.857 and the AUC of 0.935. Conversely, the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model was less accurate, efficient but limited vocabulary and more OOV. All in all, the comparison illustrates that mBERT and XLM-RoBERTa are the best models to be used in detecting abusive language with robust multi-linguistic support and this explains why they can be used in real-life content moderation tools.

title: Hybrid adversarial distilled defense for deep learning-based breast cancer detection
abstract: Abstract Deep learning models have demonstrated remarkable potential in breast cancer detection, yet their vulnerability to adversarial attacks raises significant concerns for clinical deployment. This study proposes a novel hybrid adversarial distillation framework that integrates ensemble adversarial training with knowledge distillation to develop a robust yet computationally efficient breast cancer detection model. We first establish the extreme vulnerability of standard deep learning models to adversarial perturbations, demonstrating accuracy drops from 99.69% to near-zero under projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. To address this, we develop an ensemble teacher model combining DenseNet121, ResNet50, and EfficientNet-B0 trained adversarially on fast gradient sign method (FGSM)-perturbed images. Knowledge from this robust teacher is then distilled into a lightweight ResNet18 student model through a specialized loss function balancing cross-entropy and Kullback–Leibler divergence. Extensive evaluations show that our distilled model maintains near 60% accuracy under strong FGSM attacks and, remarkably, 58.50% accuracy against PGD attacks ( ε = 0.3, α = 0.01, 10 iterations), where both baseline and ensemble models fail completely. Under stronger attack setting (50 iterations), the model continues to maintain meaningful accuracy, indicating robustness beyond the standard PGD configuration. Furthermore, the distilled model demonstrates superior resistance to transfer attacks, maintaining over 70% accuracy against examples crafted on the teacher model. While the trade-off reduces clean-data accuracy to 78.88%, our approach provides a computationally efficient solution for securing breast cancer detection systems against adversarial manipulation. This work represents a significant step toward clinically viable, secure AI-based diagnostic tools, though future work should focus on further improving clean-data accuracy while maintaining robust adversarial defenses.

title: LinuxArena: A Control Setting for AI Agents in Live Production Software Environments
abstract: We introduce LinuxArena, a control setting in which agents operate directly on live, multi-service production environments. LinuxArena contains 20 environments, 1,671 main tasks representing legitimate software engineering work, and 184 side tasks representing safety failures such as data exfiltration and backdooring, making it the largest and most diverse control setting for software engineering to date. We validate LinuxArena is useful for control research by running sabotage evaluations, which measure whether attackers can complete side tasks while working on main tasks, and monitor evaluations, which measure a monitor model's ability to detect sabotage attempts. Against a GPT-5-nano trusted monitor at a 1\% step-wise false positive rate, Claude Opus 4.6 achieves roughly a 23% undetected sabotage success rate. We additionally release LaStraj, a dataset of human-crafted attack trajectories that evade monitors at substantially higher rates than any model-generated attacks we elicited, showing that current attack policies do not saturate LinuxArena. These results suggest that LinuxArena has meaningful headroom for both attackers and defenders, making it a strong testbed for developing and evaluating future control protocols.

title: TrigReason: Trigger-Based Collaboration between Small and Large Reasoning Models
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) achieve strong performance on complex tasks through extended chains of thought but suffer from high inference latency due to autoregressive reasoning. Recent work explores using Small Reasoning Models (SRMs) to accelerate LRM inference. In this paper, we systematically characterize the capability boundaries of SRMs and identify three common types of reasoning risks: (1) path divergence, where SRMs lack the strategic ability to construct an initial plan, causing reasoning to deviate from the most probable path; (2) cognitive overload, where SRMs fail to solve particularly difficult steps; and (3) recovery inability, where SRMs lack robust self-reflection and error correction mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose TrigReason, a trigger-based collaborative reasoning framework that replaces continuous polling with selective intervention. TrigReason delegates most reasoning to the SRM and activates LRM intervention only when necessary-during initial strategic planning (strategic priming trigger), upon detecting extraordinary overconfidence (cognitive offload trigger), or when reasoning falls into unproductive loops (intervention request trigger). The evaluation results on AIME24, AIME25, and GPQA-D indicate that TrigReason matches the accuracy of full LRMs and SpecReason, while offloading 1.70x - 4.79x more reasoning steps to SRMs. Under edge-cloud conditions, TrigReason reduces latency by 43.9\% and API cost by 73.3\%. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/QQQ-yi/TrigReason}{https://github.com/QQQ-yi/TrigReason}

title: Supplementary Prompt Material for "Evaluating Prompt Strategies for LLM-Based De-Identification of German Discharge Letters: A Feasibility Study Using GraSCCo"
abstract: This repository contains the prompt material used in the study “Evaluating Prompt Strategies for LLM-Based De-Identification of German Discharge Letters: A Feasibility Study Using GraSCCo,” accepted as a full paper at ICIMTH 2026. The document includes the German prompts used for the baseline, session-isolated, structured-input, and optimized-prompt setups, as well as English translations for readability. The German prompts represent the experimentally evaluated versions. The English translations were not evaluated experimentally and are provided only to support transparency and international interpretation of the prompt design. The prompts were developed for de-identification of synthetic German discharge letters from the GraSCCo corpus using the GeMTeX de-identification guideline.

title: Reasoning Topology Evolution: Automated Discovery of Effective Reasoning DAG Structures for LLM Agents
abstract: This paper introduces Reasoning Topology Evolution (RTE), a framework that applies evolutionary algorithms to discover reasoning graph structures for large language model (LLM) agents. While Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thought, and Graph-of-Thought use fixed human-designed topologies, RTE evolves the topology itself. Reasoning strategies are encoded as directed acyclic graphs (Reasoning Genomes) where nodes represent reasoning operations and edges represent information flow. The evolutionary search starts from only linear chains and random DAGs with no hand-designed multi-path seeds. Across five independent runs on Qwen-2.5-1.5B-Instruct, evolution discovers topologies achieving 0.720 accuracy on a 50-problem held-out set, significantly outperforming linear Chain-of-Thought (0.420, p < 0.001) and random DAGs (0.360, p < 0.001), while matching hand-designed Tree-of-Thought (0.720). The fitness landscape is multimodal: different runs discover structurally distinct yet comparably effective topologies. Code, results, and all figures are included.

title: Automated Detection of Pelvic Bone Metastases in Radionuclide Bone Scan Images Using a Dual-Stream Cross-Attention Transformer Model
abstract: The detection of pelvic bone metastasis using radionuclide bone scintigraphy is challenging due to complex anatomical structures and intense urinary bladder uptake, which reduces diagnostic accuracy and creates inter-observer variability. This paper presents a Dual-Stream Cross-Attention Vision Transformer (DSCAVT) model that automatically detects pelvic bone metastasis by simultaneously analyzing anterior and posterior views of bone scans. To enhance diagnostic accuracy, the proposed approach incorporates domain-specific preprocessing techniques, including automated bladder masking, morphological top-hat enhancement, sigmoid-based intensity normalization, and multi-channel image construction. Two Vision Transformer encoders extract global features from each view employ cross-attention mechanisms to perform mutual validation between the views. The model was tested on five-fold stratified cross-validation by using pelvic images in the BS-80k database which is publicly available. On average, we achieve accuracy of 80.3%, where ROC-AUC of$\mathbf{0. 8 3 6}$, sensitivity of 74.7%, and specificity of 81.1% are recorded from our experimental model. The cross-attention mechanism exchange pattern information, which enhance diagnostic reliability across diverse cancer type. These finding introduce that our proposed dual-view cross-attention transformer enhances pelvic metastasis detection and provides a reliable computer-aided diagnostic tool for nuclear medicine procedures.

title: Hateful Meme Identification: A Dual-Stage Multimodal Framework for the Bengali Context
abstract: Automated content moderation for social media memes (images with text) is particularly difficult due to the rapid growth of this type of content. This problem is worsened in lowresourced languages (e.g., Bengali) where sarcasm, culture-based idioms, and stereotype use often serve to obscure the hateful intent in a meme. This paper proposes a two-stage multimodal framework for (1) detecting if a meme is hate and (2) more precisely classifying these memes into 9 subcategories of hate. We construct and publicly release a manually annotated dataset of 5,000 Bengali memes. We achieve strong interannotator agreement$(\kappa>0.80)$. The hateful subset, containing 2,500 memes, includes nine categories: Celebrity-targeted, Political Hate, Religion-targeted, Racism, Misogyny, Nationalistic Propaganda, Sports Hate, Vulgar Language, and Explicit Sexual Content. Our framework integrates OCR-based text extraction with transfer-learning visual encoders and transformer-based language models, followed by multimodal fusion. Our experimental results show that the proposed dual-stage model significantly outperforms unimodal baselines. It achieves an F1-score of$\mathbf{0. 8 4}$for binary detection. The multimodal fusion approach achieves 83.2 % accuracy with a macro-F1 of 0.79, for nine-class classification. Comprehensive ablation and error analyses further highlight the effectiveness of multimodal learning in low-resource settings.

title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Topology-Preserving Diffusion Oversampling (UTP-DO) for Imbalanced Learning
abstract: Class imbalance has been an inherent problem in supervised learning, and it results in biased classifiers and ineffective generalization on minorities. Current methods of oversampling, such as interpolation-based and adversarial generative models, are both ineffective at capturing the underlying geometry of minority data distributions as well as unstable and prone to mode collapse. To address these shortcomings, the current paper introduces an Uncertainty-Calibrated Topology-Preserving Diffusion Oversampling (UTP-DO) architecture for imbalanced learning. The proposed method redefines minority augmentation as conditional generative modelling issue in latent representation space. To estimate predictive uncertainty at the sample level, predictive uncertainty is first estimated through a deep classifier continuously. The scores of these uncertainties are then used as conditioning signals in a diffusion-based generative model that generates minority embeddings with better mode coverage and stability. Manifold distortion should be avoided, and a topology-respecting regularization mechanism is proposed, which is based on graph Laplacian image constraints and density-consistency alignment, and ensures that synthetic samples do not lose the local structure of the neighbourhood or the overall geometric structure of the geometry. The last classifier is trained using the augmented dataset, which consists of the real instances and the topology-consistent synthetic samples. The comprehensive testing of numerous benchmark data sets shows that the proposed framework achieves higher results than state-of-the-art SMOTE variants and GAN-based augmentation algorithms in terms of F1-score, G-mean, and balanced accuracy. The findings show that geometry-sensitive diffusion-based augmentation is a strong and scalable method of AI-based imbalanced data classification.
