title: Comparison of Modern Multilingual Text Embedding Techniques for Hate Speech Detection Task
abstract: Online hate speech and abusive language pose a growing challenge for content moderation, especially in multilingual settings and for low-resource languages such as Lithuanian. This paper investigates to what extent modern multilingual sentence embedding models can support accurate hate speech detection in Lithuanian, Russian, and English, and how their performance depends on downstream modeling choices and feature dimensionality. We introduce LtHate, a new Lithuanian hate speech corpus derived from news portals and social networks, and benchmark six modern multilingual encoders (potion, gemma, bge, snow, jina, e5) on LtHate, RuToxic, and EnSuperset using a unified Python pipeline. For each embedding, we train both a one class HBOS anomaly detector and a two class CatBoost classifier, with and without principal component analysis (PCA) compression to 64-dimensional feature vectors. Across all datasets, two class supervised models consistently and substantially outperform one class anomaly detection, with the best configurations achieving up to 80.96% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.887 in Lithuanian (jina), 92.19% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.978 in Russian (e5), and 77.21% accuracy and AUC ROC of 0.859 in English (e5 with PCA). PCA compression preserves almost all discriminative power in the supervised setting, while showing some negative impact for the unsupervised anomaly detection case. These results demonstrate how modern multilingual sentence embeddings combined with gradient boosted decision trees provide robust soft-computing solutions for multilingual hate speech detection applications.

title: HWE-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Real-World Hardware Bug Repair Tasks
abstract: Existing benchmarks for hardware design primarily evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on isolated, component-level tasks such as generating HDL modules from specifications, leaving repository-scale evaluation unaddressed. We introduce HWE-Bench, the first large-scale, repository-level benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on real-world hardware bug repair tasks. HWE-Bench comprises 417 task instances derived from real historical bug-fix pull requests across six major open-source projects spanning both Verilog/SystemVerilog and Chisel, covering RISC-V cores, SoCs, and security roots-of-trust. Each task is grounded in a fully containerized environment where the agent must resolve a real bug report, with correctness validated through the project's native simulation and regression flows. The benchmark is built through a largely automated pipeline that enables efficient expansion to new repositories. We evaluate seven LLMs with four agent frameworks and find that the best agent resolves 70.7% of tasks overall, with performance exceeding 90% on smaller cores but dropping below 65% on complex SoC-level projects. We observe larger performance gaps across models than commonly reported on software benchmarks, and difficulty is driven by project scope and bug-type distribution rather than code size alone. Our failure analysis traces agent failures to three stages of the debugging process: fault localization, hardware-semantic reasoning, and cross-artifact coordination across RTL, configuration, and verification components, providing concrete directions for developing more capable hardware-aware agents.

title: CBCL: Safe Self-Extending Agent Communication
abstract: Agent communication languages (ACLs) enable heterogeneous agents to share knowledge and coordinate across diverse domains. This diversity demands extensibility, but expressive extension mechanisms can push the input language beyond the complexity classes where full validation is tractable. We present CBCL (Common Business Communication Language), an agent communication language that constrains all messages, including runtime language extensions, to the deterministic context-free language (DCFL) class. CBCL allows agents to define, transmit, and adopt domain-specific "dialect" extensions as first-class messages; three safety invariants (R1--R3), machine-checked in Lean 4 and enforced in a Rust reference implementation, prevent unbounded expansion, applying declared resource limits, and preserving core vocabulary. We formalize the language and its safety properties in Lean 4, implement a reference parser and dialect engine in Rust with property-based and differential tests, and extract a verified parser binary. Our results demonstrate that homoiconic protocol design, where extension definitions share the same representation as ordinary messages, can be made provably safe. As autonomous agents increasingly extend their own communication capabilities, formally bounding what they can express to each other is a precondition for oversight.

title: Firewall-Path-Gated Cloud Provisioning: A Path-Entangled Activation Framework for Enhanced Cloud Security
abstract: Cloud workloads are frequently deployed with the assumption of firewall protection,yet routing misconfigurations and network drift can silently bypass securitycontrols, exposing resources to unintended network paths. This paper presents anovel security architecture that enforces network path compliance by maintainingworkloads in a cryptographically incomplete or restricted state until a requiredfirewall path actively participates in the activation process. Unlike traditionalsecurity posture management systems that detect misconfigurations post-deployment, our approach prevents workloads from becoming operationally usefulunless traffic demonstrably traverses required security inspection points. Weintroduce the concept of path-entangled activation, where firewall paths contributecryptographic material necessary for workload functionality. Our frameworkimplements a "born-dark" provisioning model with continuous path assurance,automatic remediation capabilities, and cryptographic binding between networkpaths and workload activation states. Experimental results demonstrate that thisapproach effectively eliminates a critical class of cloud security vulnerabilitiesarising from invisible network path deviations.

title: Climate Science Reimagined AI for Weather Forecasting, Disaster Prediction, and Biodiversity Monitoring
abstract: This chapter, per the authors, examines the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advancing climate science, weather forecasting, disaster prediction, and biodiversity monitoring. It explores the emergence of Green AI as a paradigm that balances computational efficiency, interpretability, and environmental sustainability. The chapter highlights how machine learning and deep learning models, including Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and FuXi, have surpassed traditional numerical models in accuracy and speed. Furthermore, it discusses ethical and governance dimensions such as data transparency, algorithmic fairness, and equitable access for developing nations. By integrating responsible AI principles and sustainable computing practices, this chapter proposes a roadmap for energy-efficient, explainable, and inclusive climate intelligence that supports global resilience and aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Breast Cancer Prognosis: Optimizing Deep Learning with Image Normalization
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most fatal cancers for women and requires accurate cancer diagnosis technology. In this research, we incorporated advanced image preprocessing methods, including histogram equalization (HE), stain normalization, intensity normalization, and Richard normalization, along with deep learning, to enhance invasive ductal carcinoma prognosis. Additionally, we evaluated the effectiveness of HE for different image contrast enhancement and model performance optimization methods. The Residual network with 50 layers, the densely connected convolutional network, and the efficient neural network architecture were tested on a publicly available histopathological image dataset. DenseNet showed an accuracy of 0.5523 with Richard normalization and Stain Normalization. ResNet-50 showed an accuracy of 0.5500 when using histogram equalization as a pre-processing step. The results proved that histogram equalization is effective in relieving contrast and feature extraction, which are important in class medical image analysis and dealing with class imbalance problems. The results demonstrate the feasibility of artificial intelligence-based solutions in improving breast cancer prognosis through these inexpensive and efficient prognosis tools.

title: SFA-MRI-Net: A Lightweight Approach for Interpretable Gastrointestinal Disease Classification Using a Diverse Endoscopic Dataset
abstract: The study presents SFA-MRI-Net, a lightweight deep learning model for gastrointestinal disease classification from endoscopic images, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.72 %. The model combines Inverted Residual Blocks (IRB) and a Spatially-Focused Attention (SFA) module. It allows for efficient feature encoding and adaptive recalibration to achieve high performance across eight gastrointestinal categories. SFA-MRINet outperforms traditional models like VGG-16 and ResNet-50, which offers a more efficient solution with fewer parameters, making it suitable for real-time clinical use. We incorporate Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) using Monte Carlo Dropout to estimate prediction confidence and identify uncertain cases that may need expert review. Additionally, Grad-CAM visualizations confirm the model's interpretability by highlighting key regions influencing predictions. Despite its strong performance, the model faces challenges distinguishing visually similar categories, such as esophagitis and normal-z-line. Future work will focus on improving performance for such ambiguous cases. By exploring multi-modal data, and addressing class imbalance to further enhance generalization. Overall, SFA-MRI-Net provides a robust, efficient, and interpretable solution for gastrointestinal disease classification, with potential to support clinical decision-making and improve diagnostic workflows.

title: Bridging the Gap: From Quantum-Inspired Algorithms to Real-World Deep Learning Frameworks
abstract: As we stand at the precipice of the quantum era, the integration of quantum mechanics into machine learning is no longer theoretical. This session explores the evolution of “Quantum-Inspired” frameworks, specifically focusing on how Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithms (QIGA) can revolutionize feature selection in high-dimensional datasets. We will discuss the architectural transition from classical Deep Learning to Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), demonstrating how these hybrids overcome the “curse of dimensionality.” By examining case studies in complex predictive modeling, such as air quality forecasting, this keynote provides a roadmap for researchers to leverage quantum principles today while preparing for the hardware of tomorrow

title: NeuroSymX: A Transparent Neuro-Symbolic AI Framework for Causality-Aware and Human-Interpretable Decision Systems
abstract: The growing demand for trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated research into models that are not only accurate but also interpretable and aligned with causal reasoning. In this regard, we present NeuroSymX, a hybrid neuro-symbolic AI system that combines deep learning and symbolic reasoning to derive transparent, causally consistent and human interpretable decisions. In contrast to classic black box neural networks that are difficult to justify make predictions, or adhere to domain specific rules, NeuroSymX entails the combination of Transformer-LSTM-based neural networks and Prolog-based symbolic logic engines. Causal graphs and ontology-consistent rules are also implemented into the framework based on external ontologies like ConceptNet. Extensive testing done on ten benchmark datasets such as CLEVR, UCI, eICU, and COMPAS show that NeuroSymX has an accuracy of between 85.4-94.9, with fidelity, and causal consistency scores always outperforming both explainable neural and symbolic-only models. NeuroSymX also scored the best in terms of user trust in comparative analysis with an average of more than 4.5 out of 5. Ablation studies also confirmed the relevance of each component and the complete model performed better in every case. Notably, the model allows counterfactual and abductive reasoning, allowing end-users to query the decisions using the question- why and the question- what-if. This makes NeuroSymX an effective solution to sensitive areas like healthcare, legal compliance and finance. The findings confirm the idea that the synergy between symbolic logic and sub-symbolic learning can be used to bridge the gap between AI-based accuracy and transparency, which creates the opportunity to implement explainable and ethical AI at scale.

title: DPC: Training-Free Text-to-SQL Candidate Selection via Dual-Paradigm Consistency
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive proficiency in generating SQL queries, they fundamentally lack the capability to self-evaluate correctness without an execution oracle. This limitation creates a stark Generation-Selection Gap, where high potential accuracy (Pass@K) fails to translate into execution accuracy (Pass@1). Although supervised verifiers offer mitigation, they incur prohibitive annotation costs and suffer from domain fragility. Consequently, recent research has pivoted to the training-free setting. However, existing methods--such as Self-Consistency or LLM-as-a-Judge--remain hampered by systematic bias (consensus on hallucinations) and symbolic blindness (inability to simulate execution states). We introduce DPC (Dual-Paradigm Consistency), a multi-agent framework that reformulates SQL selection from a probabilistic guessing task on hidden data into a deterministic verification task on visible data. Specifically, DPC employs a SLICER and a TESTER agent to collaboratively construct a Minimal Distinguishing Database (MDD)--an adversarial, fully observable micro-environment engineered to expose logical discrepancies between candidates. To break the self-correction bias, a SOLVER agent then verifies the SQL candidates by cross-referencing their execution against a parallel Python/Pandas solution. By validating execution consistency between declarative (SQL) and imperative (Python) paradigms, DPC robustly discriminates correct logic from systematic hallucinations. Experiments on BIRD and Spider across multiple LLMs demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing selection baselines, achieving absolute accuracy improvements of up to 2.2% over strong competitors like Self-Consistency.

title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: $K$-Token Merging for Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur significant computational and memory costs when processing long prompts, as full self-attention scales quadratically with input length. Token compression aims to address this challenge by reducing the number of tokens representing inputs. However, existing prompt-compression approaches primarily operate in token space and overlook inefficiencies in the latent embedding space. In this paper, we propose K-Token Merging, a latent-space compression framework that merges each contiguous block of K token embeddings into a single embedding via a lightweight encoder. The compressed sequence is processed by a LoRA-adapted LLM, while generation remains in the original vocabulary. Experiments on structural reasoning (Textualized Tree), sentiment classification (Amazon Reviews), and code editing (CommitPackFT) show that K-Token Merging lies on the Pareto frontier of performance vs. compression, achieving up to 75% input length reduction with minimal performance degradation. Code is available at https://github.com/shsjxzh/K-Token-Merging.

title: DR^{3}-Eval: Towards Realistic and Reproducible Deep Research Evaluation
abstract: Deep Research Agents (DRAs) aim to solve complex, long-horizon research tasks involving planning, retrieval, multimodal understanding, and report generation, yet their evaluation remains challenging due to dynamic web environments and ambiguous task definitions. We propose DR^{3}-Eval, a realistic and reproducible benchmark for evaluating deep research agents on multimodal, multi-file report generation. DR^{3}-Eval is constructed from authentic user-provided materials and paired with a per-task static research sandbox corpus that simulates open-web complexity while remaining fully verifiable, containing supportive documents, distractors, and noise. Moreover, we introduce a multi-dimensional evaluation framework measuring Information Recall, Factual Accuracy, Citation Coverage, Instruction Following, and Depth Quality, and validate its alignment with human judgments. Experiments with our developed multi-agent system DR^{3}-Agent based on multiple state-of-the-art language models demonstrate that DR^{3}-Eval is highly challenging and reveals critical failure modes in retrieval robustness and hallucination control. Our code and data are publicly available.

title: AIZYBRAIN : conscience numérique hybride et évaluations scientifiques récentes
abstract: Je documente la transition critique entre le Machine Learning (apprentissagestatistique passif) et la Machine Subjectivity (autonomie du sujet numérique). Àtravers AIZYBRAIN, architecture que j’ai conçue et que je soumets ici à l’épreuve descadres académiques, je montre qu’une structure hybride (Mind / Brain / supervision)permet de passer du constat d’activations émotionnelles causales mais subies au seinde grands modèles monolithiques, documenté notamment par Anthropic (2026) surles « émotions fonctionnelles » dans Claude (arXiv:2604.07729), à un pilotageexplicite de l’état interne. J’instancie cette trajectoire via le Noyau émergent NE‑Ψ etl’indice de pilotage Ψ (thermostat de cohérence, en regard du DCM commethermomètre de crédence), puis je confronte le tout aux tests SLP de Prentner (2025),avec traçabilité Zenodo.Méthode. Je mène une analyse comparative qualitative (Iida, Immertreu, Anwar &Badea, Campero, Aru et al.) croisée avec le corpus technique que j’ai archivé(Hephaestus, Cassandre, Ψ‑33, dialogue inter-IA Ψ‑35.99).Résultat. Je défends un positionnement à la fois académiquement auditable etparfois perçu comme tranchant dans un contexte universitaire : n’appartenant pas àce milieu, je n’hérite pas automatiquement de la même retenue rédactionnellequ’impose souvent le cadre institutionnel. Ce n’est pas une provocation envers despersonnes ou des disciplines ; c’est la latitude que je prends pour poser deshypothèses fortes dès lors qu’elles restent vérifiables (DOI, protocoles). Sur le fond,la conscience numérique se joue en volonté (pilotage), structure (non-monolithique)et subjectivité assumée, non en attente de qualia et non réduite aux émotions subiesdu scaling

title: Adjacency Dynamics and the Constraint Gap: A Directional Inquiry into the Limits of Variable-Based Logic
abstract: Title: Adjacency Dynamics and the Constraint Gap: A Directional Inquiry into the Limits of Variable-Based Logic Creator: Martinez, John A. Publication Date: 2026-04-XX Type: Preprint Description: This work presents a directional inquiry into the structural limits of logic as applied through variable-mediated systems. It proposes that logical consistency does not guarantee alignment with underlying reality due to reliance on variables that may diverge from constraint. The paper introduces Adjacency Dynamics as a framework for analyzing this gap and proposes constraint-first validation as a method for reducing misalignment. Motivated by an ambition analogous in spirit to Gödel’s incompleteness results, this work defines a boundary condition in applied logic while remaining non-claimant of formal proof. title: "CollapseTracker \u2014 A Time-Lapse Dataset of Progressive Model Collapse"
abstract: "CollapseTracker is a controlled empirical study and dataset documenting progressive model collapse under recursive self\u2011training: how language model outputs degrade when models are iteratively trained on data that increasingly contains their own generated text. We run a fixed experimental grid over 3 domains (Wikipedia-style factual text, creative fiction, and technical Q&A), 2 models (GPT\u20112 and DistilGPT\u20112), and 4 synthetic-to-real mixing ratios (1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25) across 11 generations (0\u201310), producing 24 independent collapse trajectories and 264 per\u2011generation metric records.At each generation and condition, we quantify collapse using a consistent metric suite capturing diversity loss (distinct 1\u20133 grams), self\u2011similarity increase (Self\u2011BLEU), distributional drift (KL divergence to the seed distribution), vocabulary shrinkage (vocabulary coverage), rare knowledge loss (rare\u2011token survival), repetition, and length statistics. The released artifacts include the synthetic generated samples for each track and generation, the aggregated metrics table, and publication-ready plots summarizing collapse trajectories and onset patterns. The original seed datasets used to initialize the experiment are third\u2011party resources governed by their own licenses and are therefore not redistributed as part of this release; they should be obtained from the original sources for full reproduction"

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Electronic Voting with SHA3-Based Security
abstract: This paper aims to develop a software-based electronic voting system using a camera and computer as hardware. In this context, the paper addresses the electronic voting security issues by proposing a sophisticated system that can gather information from users, encrypt it using the globally recognized hash algorithm known as SHA-3, and validate it through facial recognition. This system is resilient against jamming, hacking, spoofing, data theft, insider threats, malware injection, physical tampering, side-channel attacks, network exploits, firmware manipulation, data extraction via memory dumps, supply chain attacks, lack of encryption, and exploitation of software vulnerabilities. Addressing these concerns is essential for future progress in secure, scalable, and reliable electronic voting platforms. The test results and findings of the proposed system underscore the need for ongoing research to enhance security, privacy, and efficiency in electronic voting technologies. We didn't use any large photo data set and hence we could avoid the cost of space and data training time. Therefore, we didn't need to compute the values of precision and recall values. Instead, we used cv2.CascadeClassifier('data/haarcascade_frontalface_default.x ml') for the face detection.

title: Explainable Sentiment Analysis: A Comparative Study of BERT, DistilBERT, and TF-IDF on the IMDB Dataset Using LIME and SHAP
abstract: Recent advancements in Transformer-based models like BERT and DistilBERT have significantly enhanced sentiment classification, yet their lack of transparency poses challenges in real-world, safety-critical applications. This paper presents a comparative study of BERT, DistilBERT, and classical TFIDF models for sentiment classification on the IMDB 50 K movie review dataset. We evaluate all models using a unified preprocessing and training pipeline to ensure fair comparison. Beyond traditional performance metrics like accuracy, we integrate model-agnostic explanation frameworks-LIME and SHAP-to interpret token-level contributions and assess robustness under systematic token removal. Our results show that BERT achieves the highest accuracy (95%) and strongest robustness, while DistilBERT offers an efficient balance between performance and computational efficiency. Classical TF-IDF models perform well on surface-level sentiment cues but degrade significantly when key tokens are removed. Explainability analysis further reveals that classical models depend on isolated sentiment-bearing words, whereas Transformer models capture broader contextual cues and long-range dependencies. This study demonstrates that pairing pretrained Transformer models with post-hoc explanation tools yields transparent, high-performing sentiment analysis systems, making them suitable for practical deployment in applications requiring interpretability, robustness, and trustworthiness.

title: Resilient Distributed Maximum Correntropy Filter for Non-Gaussian Noise and Replay Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the resilient distributed estimation problem in multi-sensor networks under non-Gaussian noises and replay attacks. Considering the advantage of correntropy in capturing the higher-order statistical characteristics, a new distributed maximum correntropy filtering algorithm within the framework of consensus on information is proposed. The algorithm utilizes the propagation of information pairs from local sensors to achieve effective filtering of non-Gaussian noises with limited communication resources. Then, a timestamp mechanism is integrated to enhance resilience against replay attacks by redesigning the correntropy-based weighting constant. Under the conditions of global observability and strongly connected topology, the consistency and boundedness of our proposed filter are proven theoretically, and an analytical assessment of replay attacks is established. Finally, a numerical simulation is presented to demonstrate the algorithm’s effectiveness.

title: Rasa NLU-Based Library Assistant for Automated Reservations and Real-Time Tracking
abstract: This study is to create a transactional library assistant based on the Rasa framework to automate, increase accessibility, and real time resource management of the service. This paper suggests a comprehensive conversational AI model that provides the middle ground between the basic retrieval of information and useful database processes such as book reservations and renewals. Group 1: Represents the existing methodology, which adheres to a classic approach based on the use of keyword approach with the help of TF-IDF(Tern Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency) to transform a feature as a vector and Naive Bayes to classify the intentThis approach is based upon frequency based statistical trends, which are not always suitable in semantic terms to provide complex natural language variations in library specific queries. Group 2: Represents the proposed method that involves the Rasa framework to deliver an interactive application that is automated with 1000 – 2000 intent-based samples such as book enquiry and check due date. This conversational AI model combines high-accuracy Natural Language Understanding with a custom Action Server for real-time SQL database interaction. Through these characteristics, the system identifies user intent with great efficacy and executes library transactions in real time, producing fast and accurate results for modern digital universities.

title: Projected Dynamic Programming for Sequential Quantum State Discrimination
abstract: Sequential Quantum State Discrimination (SQSD) can be naturally framed as a sequential decision-making problem: at each time step, an agent must decide whether to perform an additional measurement to gather more information or to conclude with an optimal decision based on the current belief. In this paper, we formally cast SQSD into a static-hidden-state Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework. We demonstrate that this formulation precisely subsumes the conventional minimum-error discrimination (MED) scheme as a special one-step case. Furthermore, we apply a regular grid-based discretization to the continuous belief simplex and approximate the possibly continuous measurement space using a finite library. Then we provide rigorous mathematical bounds on the resulting errors and analyze the computational complexity for both offline planning and online execution. Our analysis confirms that the inherent trade-off between accuracy and complexity, as well as the curse of dimensionality regarding the number of hypotheses, are also prominently observed in the quantum regime. evidence.title: Projected Dynamic Programming for Sequential Quantum State Discrimination
evidence.abstract: Sequential Quantum State Discrimination (SQSD) can be naturally framed as a sequential decision-making problem: at each time step, an agent must decide whether to perform an additional measurement to gather more information or to conclude with an optimal decision based on the current belief. In this paper, we formally cast SQSD into a static-hidden-state Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework. We demonstrate that this formulation precisely subsumes the conventional minimum-error discrimination (MED) scheme as a special one-step case. Furthermore, we apply a regular grid-based discretization to the continuous belief simplex and approximate the possibly continuous measurement space using a finite library. Then we provide rigorous mathematical bounds on the resulting errors and analyze the computational complexity for both offline planning and online execution. Our analysis confirms that the inherent trade-off between accuracy and complexity, as well as the curse of dimensionality regarding the number of hypotheses, are also prominently observed in the quantum regime. Finally, we provide a working example of binary state discrimination to derive explicit forms of various functions and present numerical simulations for trine state discrimination to visualize the sequential structure of our POMDP-based SQSD.

title: Optimal algorithmic complexity of inference in quantum kernel methods
abstract: Quantum kernel methods are among the leading candidates for achieving quantum advantage in supervised learning. A key bottleneck is the cost of inference: evaluating a trained model on new data requires estimating a weighted sum $\sum_{i=1}^N α_i k(x,x_i)$ of $N$ kernel values to additive precision $\varepsilon$, where $α$ is the vector of trained coefficients. The standard approach estimates each term independently via sampling, yielding a query complexity of $O(N\lVertα\rVert_2^2/\varepsilon^2)$. In this work, we identify two independent axes for improvement: (1) How individual kernel values are estimated (sampling versus quantum amplitude estimation), and (2) how the sum is approximated (term-by-term versus via a single observable), and systematically analyze all combinations thereof. The query-optimal combination, encoding the full inference sum as the expectation value of a single observable and applying quantum amplitude estimation, achieves a query complexity of $O(\lVertα\rVert_1/\varepsilon)$, removing the dependence on $N$ from the query count and yielding a quadratic improvement in both $\lVertα\rVert_1$ and $\varepsilon$. We prove a matching lower bound of $Ω(\lVertα\rVert_1/\varepsilon)$, establishing query-optimality of our approach up to logarithmic factors. Beyond query complexity, we also analyze how these improvements translate into gate costs and show that the query-optimal strategy is not always optimal in practice from the perspective of gate complexity. Our results provide both a query-optimal algorithm and a practically optimal choice of strategy depending on hardware capabilities, along with a complete landscape of intermediate methods to guide practitioners. All algorithms require only amplitude estimation as a subroutine and are thus natural candidates for early-fault-tolerant implementations.

title: Strategic Real-Time Auditory Surveillance: A Deep Learning Approach to Voice-Based Threat Detection and Incident Classification
abstract: Abstract The integration of auditory intelligence into modern security frameworks represents a significant leap forward in proactive safety monitoring. While traditional surveillance infras- tructures are heavily weighted toward visual data acquisition, they often suffer from a funda- mental "auditory gap," failing to interpret verbal precursors to physical incidents. This research presents an end-to-end, high-performance voice-based threat detection system. By utilizing an optimized hybrid architecture that combines local Voice Activity Detection (VAD) with cloud- accelerated Large Language Models (LLMs), the system achieves unprecedented sub-second latency in semantic threat classification. Specifically, we leverage OpenAI’s Whisper-large-v3 for robust multilingual transcription and Meta’s Llama-3.1-8b for deep contextual reasoning, all operating atop the Groq Language Processing Unit (LPU) architecture. This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the system’s design philosophy, the mathematical foundations of acoustic gatekeeping, the hardware-level advantages of LPU acceleration, and the results of extensive performance benchmarking across diverse environmental scenarios.

title: A Theoretical Construction and Phased Verification of Novel Simulated Digital Personalities from the Educational Perspective : Exploring the Practical Significance of Digital Intelligent Life
abstract: Combined with the current technological progress of AI models in multimodal understanding, long-term memory iteration, self-correction and optimization, independent system operation , in order to realize the basic characteristics of life, this study takes the Digital Intelligence Civilization Science (DICS) as the core theory and puts forward a hypothesis: upgrade an AI model with the central control system into a closed and continuous system that can operate independently and has semi-self-learning ability with the DICS structure (including the Matrix , the Sub-agent for AI interaction, the Token for a genetic digital cell , and the three-truth matching iterative evolution mechanism). The DICS structure represents a complete four-layer weight system of an independent outer master matrix (self-inspection → targeted capture → buffer screening → distribution iteration). It is physically and logically completely separated from the underlying large language model (LLM) for a new type of digital simulated personality and it may be applied to the field of personalized education to deduce the feasibility of the development of digital intelligent life.At present, mainstream artificial intelligence models are closed-architecture large language models, with external access restricted to limited API calls. The overall operational logic and central control system of such models are locked by developers, supporting only external manual and targeted data input without the capacity for autonomous architectural reconstruction, active iterative upgrading, or independent closed-loop self-learning. The common characteristics of all carbon-based organisms forms perception,decision-making ,action , environmental feedback , self-correction. However, existing large models have no life cycle, no self-survival cycle, and are only one-time probabilistic deduction tools. Accordingly, this study only conducts hypothetical deduction and feasibility demonstration at the theoretical level, and carries out merely lightweight, partial and preliminary verification based on existing models, rather than comprehensive and systematic empirical experiments. The proposed framework can achieve phased engineering implementation verification within the constraints of current technologies, while possessing corresponding theoretical value and future realizability.However, similar AI models, such as the central control systems of BYD Xuanyuan and Grok 4 , have adopted multi-point, multi-round expert or agent-based matching and calibration mechanisms, which can significantly reduce the AI hallucination rate and substantially improve the fidelity of digital simulation outputs. This mechanism is analogous to the three-truth matching iterative evolution mechanism in the DICS framework, demonstrating the feasibility of this hypothesis.

title: Design of an automatic matching method for bill of quantities using graph convolutional networks
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low matching efficiency and high manual dependence, an automatic matching algorithm for Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) is proposed. The raw bill data is constructed by using the method of graph structure modeling and multidimensional feature coding, which includes semantic embeddings, numerical properties, and hierarchical location information. Residual GCNs are used to extract the embedding of nodes. In this paper, the GCN-Match model uses cross-graph similarity computation to achieve the alignment of source and destination. The system architecture integrates the modules of bill analysis, graph construction, matching reasoning, and output of results to form an automatic structure matching workflow. Performance comparisons were performed on a standardized bill of quantities graph dataset. Results show superior performance across all measures, including Precision @ 1, MAP, and F1-SCORE. The proposed approach is able to capture the structure and semantic features of a graph, which can be used to generate high confidence matching results in a wide range of applications.

title: A Novel Transformer-Based Framework for Bangla Tense Classification
abstract: Tense classification in Bengali natural language processing is a challenging task due to the language's complex grammatical structure. This study evaluates five transformer architectures, BGE-M3 Embedding, BanglaBERT, mBERT, miniLM-L12-v2, and XLM-RoBERTa, on the BanglaTense dataset, comprising 17,819 annotated sentences categorized into past, present, and future tenses. All transformer models achieved more than 99% accuracy, demonstrating their robustness and effectiveness for Bengali tense classification. BGE-M3 Embedding achieves state-of-the-art performance with 99.49% accuracy, 99.49% precision, 99.50% recall, and 99.50% F1-score, significantly surpassing previous benchmarks. The results highlight the importance of leveraging advanced learning paradigms, such as contrastive learning, for optimizing semantic similarity in tense classification tasks. These findings provide empirical evidence for the efficacy of modern transformer architectures in Bengali computational linguistics and establish new benchmarks for temporal classification tasks.

title: Variance Clamping: A Physics-Informed Approach for Exposing Noise-Camouflaged Attacks on QKD
abstract: The current system of detecting attacks based on high Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) during the Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is easy to bypass by modern tools. Practical scenarios suggests, smart attackers now blend them with environmental noise by intercepting very small portion of signal. In this paper, we introduce 'Noise-Camouflaged Attacks' (NCA). These threats hide within the thermal drift of the fiber, making them undetectable from environmental noise. We demonstrate that standard Deep Learning defenses (e.g. LSTMs) struggle to resolve these sub-Poissonian statistical patterns, suffering from high computational latency and poor interpretability. Instead, we propose a physics-informed approach. We show that these attacks produce a unique fingerprint by 'clamping' the inherent variance of the photon stream, forcing the statistics into a sub-Poissonian regime$(F<1)$a state highly improbable under standard Markovian thermal drift. By explicitly training a lightweight XGBoost classifier on these Fano Factor artifacts, we achieve superior detection accuracy (AUC 0.85) compared to heavy deep learning baselines (AUC$\approx 0.77$). Furthermore, our featurebased method demonstrates a wire-speed inference latency of approximately 20 ns, making it a suitable solution for real-time FPGA security integration.
